title: Bootstrap
description: GET /.well-known/atlas (§9.6.1): the gateway's protocol versions and minimum, its environment, its named servers, the bindings of every built-in capability, how to sign in, and the catalogue's current ETag. Served without sign-in, with a strong ETag.

protocols.description: Every protocol version the gateway serves (§9.B).

minimum_protocol.description: The lowest protocol a client may declare; below it a call is upgrade_required (426).

environment.description: The environment's name: dv, ac, pd, local or conformance. A client accepts an emulator connect handover only when it is conformance or local (§9.7.8). It also names the sign-in file token-<environment>.json (Q-CLI-1).

servers.description: Each named server's base URL, with no trailing `/` (§9.6.1).

builtins.description: The bindings of every built-in capability of §9.3.2, keyed by its id.

catalog_etag.description: The catalogue's current ETag, as an entity-tag (with its quotes).

interactions.description: Each interaction's bindings, in preference order.

sign_in.description: How to sign in (§6.2.2, §9.7.3). Every endpoint is given, so a client never builds one (Q-DOC-2).

authority.description: The token issuer: Entra's authority, or the conformance gateway itself (§9.8.4).

client_id.description: The public client's id every Atlas client signs in as (§6.2.2).

scopes.description: The scopes to ask for; their audience is the Atlas Gateway.

token_endpoint.description: Where a refresh token is redeemed (RFC 6749 section 6, §9.7.3).

authorization_endpoint.description: Where a person signs in with PKCE (RFC 7636, RFC 8252).
